source_snapshot.procedure: Use App raw 0x06 0x59 0x00 <Parameter selector> 0x00 0x00 through localhost IB and remote OOB for selectors 0x00 Set In Progress, 0x01 System Firmware Version, 0x02 System Name, 0x03 Primary OS Name and 0x04 Present OS Name; generic logs are cleared first.
source_snapshot.criteria: Both commands succeed and response data is correct as setting, without an authoritative reference or multi-block decode.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL withholds execution for exact bytes/expected output, but calls the standard request implementation-specific and supplies no block parser.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE correctly treats the case as read-only, but reduces the listed selector coverage to one, incorrectly requires a parameter-selector echo, and repeats the historical claim that the leading 0x00 is a framing defect.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending and Source Conflict for a supposedly overlong request and missing selector/schema/reference. IPMI v2.0 section 22.14b proves the four request data bytes are correct: get-versus-revision flag, parameter selector, set selector and block selector. Table 22-16c supplies the standard response data contract. The remaining target/reference/redaction bindings are finite runtime Project configuration, not an unresolved command semantic.
disposition_reason: Preserve the original five selectors and both IB/OOB reads as separate subcases. Read revision and data with the source's correct four-byte request, decode selector 0 state, and for selectors 1-4 enumerate every required zero-based 16-byte set-selector block from the first block's encoding and byte length. Compare raw blocks across transports and decoded values with versioned Project references. This is non-mutating and needs no point-of-action confirmation, while missing runtime bindings remain NOT READY and unsupported/N/A still requires platform SPEC.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1013, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1014 were directly read; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1014 / variant e228cb226ddba862.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.14b defines request data byte 1 bit 7 as get-revision-only, byte 2 as Parameter Selector, byte 3 as Set Selector and byte 4 as Block Selector. Therefore source bytes `0x00 <selector> 0x00 0x00` are standard, not overlong.

The response is completion, Parameter Revision and configuration data; it does not echo the Parameter Selector. Standard parameters return revision 11h. A revision-only request uses first byte 80h and returns no configuration data.

Table 22-16c defines selector 0 state and selectors 1-4. Each string response carries its set-selector then a 16-byte block; first-block bytes give encoding 0 ASCII+Latin1, 1 UTF-8 or 2 Unicode and overall byte length. All blocks needed by that declared length must be retrieved, not only block zero.

Selectors 1-3 are non-volatile; selector 4 is volatile and its length is cleared by power cycle/reset. A versioned Project reference must account for legitimate lifecycle state rather than invent a universal expected string.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-13, ED-15, ED-19, ED-22, ED-26 through ED-30 and ED-33 through ED-38 preserve row/transport/selector coverage, require evidence and authoritative expected results, allow parameterized runtime bindings, prohibit log clearing and forbid blind retry.

test_case.test_name: Read and verify all standard System Info selectors over IB and OOB
test_case.purpose: Verify selectors 0-4 of standard Get System Info through the in-band interface and protected out-of-band path, reconstruct every declared string from all required blocks, and prove both transports report the same approved state without changing BMC, host, logs or System Info.
required_package: Immutable DUT/host/BMC/local-interface mapping, firmware identity, pinned ipmitool raw runner and protected OOB secret injection

Versioned IPMI 0x59 decoder that keeps the four request fields distinct, retains raw bytes, validates revision 11h, set-selector and exact response length, and decodes ASCII+Latin1, UTF-8 and Unicode safely
Versioned selector matrix for 0-4 with platform support requirement, approved expected value or authoritative source, lifecycle state, sensitivity/redaction policy and pass owner

Bounded block enumerator: first two string bytes determine encoding and byte length; retrieve at least the two standard-required storage blocks and every additional block needed for the declared length, with a configured platform maximum preventing unbounded reads
Evidence storage that preserves unredacted bytes under access control and emits only approved hashes/redacted strings in ordinary reports
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind IB and protected OOB to the same BMC and preserve logs. For each selector 0x00 through 0x04 as its own subcase, first issue `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x59 0x80 <selector> 0x00 0x00` on both paths and require a single revision byte 0x11. Issue `raw 0x06 0x59 0x00 <selector> <set-selector> 0x00`; selector 0 uses set-selector 0 and is decoded as Set In Progress. For each string selector, read set-selector 0 on both paths, require revision 0x11 plus echoed set-selector 0 and one 16-byte block, validate reserved encoding bits and byte length, then calculate the bounded block count from two metadata bytes plus the declared string byte count. Retrieve set-selectors 1..N-1 once on both paths, requiring each response to contain revision 0x11, the requested set-selector and a 16-byte block. Reassemble only the declared bytes, strictly decode encoding 0/1/2, retain padding separately, and compare both paths byte-for-byte plus the decoded value against the approved reference and lifecycle state. Never issue 0x58, clear logs, place credentials on a command line, retry automatically, reset or power cycle.
test_case.expected_result: For each selector 0-4, IB and OOB accept the correct 0x59 request and return revision 0x11 with structurally valid data. Selector 0 decodes to the same legal state on both paths. Every string selector returns the requested set-selector blocks, legal encoding and coherent byte length; complete raw blocks and decoded declared bytes match across paths and equal the approved current-state reference. No write, log deletion, reset or power event occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires all five independently identified selector subcases, both transports, the 0x80 revision-only check, revision 0x11, legal selector-0 state, exact set-selector/length/encoding checks, all required blocks, dual-path raw equality and an authoritative per-selector reference match. A zero process exit alone, only block 0, an assumed selector echo, malformed/truncated/padded-as-data response, reserved encoding/state, path mismatch or unapproved expected string is FAIL/BLOCKED as defined by the runbook. Completion 80h does not itself authorize N/A; N/A requires platform SPEC proof. If selector 0 shows an active update, preserve the read and mark the remaining snapshot BLOCKED because rollback/uncommitted semantics may make it unstable; do not poll or retry automatically.
safety_gate: Read only: prohibit App 0x58, Set In Progress changes, paired writes, log clearing, reset, power control and attempts to repair a mismatch.
Verify IB/OOB identity before comparison and protect credentials plus firmware/OS/system-name inventory according to the approved redaction policy.
Bound selector coverage to standard 0-4 and block enumeration to the decoded length and configured platform maximum; do not query OEM selectors or run an unbounded loop.
Treat selector 4 as volatile and lifecycle-dependent. Do not create a power/reset event to manufacture its expected state.
On active Set In Progress, unexpected revision, completion 80h, malformed data, path divergence or reference mismatch, collect once, stop and escalate; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/IB/OOB/tool/decoder identity, selector matrix, authoritative references and redaction policy
For each selector and transport: exact revision-only and data requests, exit/completion result, raw response hash and protected raw bytes
Selector-0 state decode; for selectors 1-4, every requested/returned set-selector, 16-byte block, encoding, declared length, padding and reconstructed value hash
Per-selector IB-versus-OOB raw comparison, decoded reference comparison, individual verdict and aggregate coverage proof for selectors 0-4
Audit proof that no 0x58, log clear, reset, power action, credential exposure or automatic retry occurred
test_case.recovery: No state change is expected and no restorative command is authorized. On failure or uncertainty, stop reads after the first bounded evidence capture, preserve protected raw output and identify target/transport/parser/reference mismatch. Do not write System Info, clear logs, reset, power cycle or retry automatically; route an active transaction to the current writer and other discrepancies to BMC/platform/inventory owners.

source_conflict.reason: The historical conflict was based on a false framing premise: IPMI 22.14b requires the source's leading 00h plus selector, set-selector and block-selector. The Review layer removes log clearing and supplies complete multi-block/reference checks while leaving the protected Master unchanged.

blocked.reason: Standard request, response, selector, encoding and block semantics are authoritative. Target mapping, platform maximum, expected values and redaction are finite runtime Project configuration; anomalous execution results are case outcomes rather than unresolved review design.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact target/IB/OOB bindings; pinned raw runner/decoder; per-selector support and authoritative current-value/lifecycle references; maximum blocks; protected secrets/evidence and redaction policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER READ-ONLY CASE ONLY; NO SYSTEM INFO, IPMI, LOG, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Section 22.14b and Tables 22-16b/c define the four request bytes, revision-only operation, response revision/data, selector-0 state, selectors 1-4, set-selector blocks, encodings, byte lengths and volatility.

project_authority: The Project BMC/inventory/OS owners bind the same target on both paths and provide versioned, lifecycle-aware references and redaction. They may document unsupported parameters for N/A but cannot replace all-selector/two-transport evidence with a successful exit code, one block, a guessed string or completion 80h alone.
